prompt: Validate package names and turn a company domain into a legal package name the way Oracle's convention says. Complete PackageNameNormalizer and run the tests.
explanation: A package segment is really just a Java identifier, so validating one is a first-character rule plus a rest-of-the-characters rule plus a keyword check. The domain convention exists because domains allow things identifiers do not -- hyphens, leading digits, and words like "new" -- so each part gets cleaned in a fixed order. Doing the digit fix after the character replacement matters: cleaning could expose a digit at the front that was not there before.
hints: Split on "\\." with a limit of -1 so an empty segment such as the one in "com..util" is not silently dropped.
Validate a segment with two loops-worth of thinking: the first character allows letters, "_" and "$"; later characters also allow digits.
In fromDomain, walk the split parts backwards and apply the clean-up steps in the documented order -- replace characters first, then fix a leading digit, then fix a reserved word.
